newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse Air says sees seasonal Q3 dip.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse Air says sees seasonal Q3 dip.

text.p: Westinghouse Air Brake Co expects a "seasonal dip" to occur in the third quarter and a return to normal levels in the fourth quarter.

President and CEO, William Kassling, said, "Currently, we expect the seasonal dip historically associated with the third quarter to occur as in the past, with a return to normal levels in the fourth quarter."

The company said it continues to implement its strategy of growth and diversification through increased content per vehicle from new product development and strategic acquisitions, international expansion and providing additional aftermarket services.
Kassling said, "We expect continued strong results from the Passenger Transit and Friction product segments during the second half of the year."

In addition, "We also anticipate that the performance of the Freight product segment will improve, as current industry estimates indicate that revenue ton miles, carloadings and intermodal traffic all show positive year-to-year comparisons," said Kassling.

"Revenues from the Electronics product segment, however, will moderate somewhat during the balance of the year, due to completion of the federal mandate that most trains be equipped with end-of-train units by July 1, 1997," added Kassling.
Kassling concluded, "Overall, we will strive to offset this shortfall in the Electronics segment with sales in other areas, but no assurances can be provided as to the eventual results."
Westinghouse Air is the largest North American producer of air brakes and related equipment for locomotives, railway freight cars and passenger transit rail vehicles.
